title: Modular VPC egress and endpoint module — dual-NAT failover, endpoint policies, route health checks
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Create a reusable Terraform module for private deployments that encapsulates multi-tier subnets, flexible egress (IGW or NAT Gateway/instance), dual-NAT active/passive failover patterns, VPC endpoint creation with policy templates, deterministic route table wiring, and built-in health checks and alarms. The module should be opinionated enough to support Redwood Private automated installs, but configurable for customers who require alternative egress or endpoint policies.
acceptance_criteria: Module creates public and private subnets across 3 AZs with predictable naming and tagging
Support for IGW-only, NAT Gateway per-AZ, and dual-NAT active/passive configurations via an input variable
Automatic creation and association of route tables for each subnet tier with explicit dependencies to avoid race conditions
VPC endpoints supported: com.amazonaws.* (S3, ECR), dynamodb, and interface endpoints with policy templates configurable per endpoint
Health checks: CloudWatch alarms and optional Lambda probe that validates egress path; failure flips NAT active flag (simulation) for canary environments
Upgrade path documented: TF 1.x provider compatibility, state migration steps when renaming resources or moving to enhanced module outputs
Integration tests in CI that run 'terraform plan' and validate output variables and at least one apply in a sandbox account
Documentation and example usage for Redwood Private and Dedicated with sample vars files
terraform_changes: Module targets Terraform 1.5+ and aws provider 5.x. Update guide included for teams on TF 1.4 -> 1.5 provider pinning
Outputs: vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, public_subnet_ids, endpoint_ids, route_table_ids (stable names for downstream modules)
State migration: resource rename map provided to move existing 'aws_route_table_association' resources to new module-managed names; step-by-step commands included
Provider aliasing recommended for multi-account installs; example in examples/ with assume_role config
rollout_plan: 1) Merge module and run CI unit tests (terraform fmt, validate, plan)
2) Deploy to sandbox account using example vars and run integration smoke tests
3) Canary private deployment: select one customer sandbox cluster with read-only traffic for 48h
4) Monitor CloudWatch alarms and cost metrics, validate no route flaps
5) Gradual rollout to production Private installs using canary policy (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
6) Post-rollout audit and add to upgrade notes
notes: Decision: use NAT Gateway for customer production by default; provide NAT instance option for very small deployments to reduce cost
Trade-off: dual-NAT active/passive increases complexity for state management and incurs extra NAT cost; acceptable for high-availability private clusters
Routing: prefer explicit route table resources per subnet with deterministic names to make future network troubleshooting and RBAC easier
Endpoint policies: provide templated JSON that can be overridden; default policy restricts S3 access to prefix used by Redwood artifacts
Health checks: initial approach uses Lambda + CloudWatch events to probe known egress endpoints; alternative (Route53 health checks) is more expensive and not always available in air-gapped installs
Follow-up: consider adding support for TGW attachment wiring in a future ticket when multi-VPC topologies are required
comments: 2025-03-07 Priya Nair: Kicked off implementation. Created module scaffold and examples directory. Verified naming conventions with infra standards.
2025-03-09 Miguel Santos: Added health probe Lambda prototype. Needs IAM review and least-privilege policy before merging.
2025-03-12 Security Review (Aisha Patel): Endpoint policy templates look good; request to surface 'sensitive_endpoints' input to force review in PR for any override.

2025-03-15 Priya Nair: Implemented dual-NAT failover primitive using CloudWatch alarm + Lambda that flips a parameter in SSM for canary tests. Will not enable by default in production until we validate failover behavior.

qa_steps: Run terraform init/validate for module with example vars (TF 1.5 provider pinned)
Apply in sandbox and verify subnets created in 3 AZs and route tables attached
Simulate NAT failure by terminating primary NAT Gateway in sandbox and verify health probe triggers failover action for dual-NAT canary
Confirm VPC endpoints created and that endpoint policy blocks/allow as per template using curl and AWS CLI
Run terraform plan for upgrade scenario from v0.8 -> v1.0 and verify state migration instructions succeed in a copy of state
monitoring: Alarms: alarm if NATGatewayActiveFlows > threshold for >5m or NATGatewayBytes drops to 0 for >2m
Health probe: Lambda running periodic HTTPS checks to known Redwood upstreams, writes custom metrics to CloudWatch
PagerDuty: urgent severity if both NATs are impaired or if endpoint creation fails during rollout
